notes: WebSearch could not be used for this part (the session's search budget was already spent), so pages were reached directly, with the kit's own User-Agent and each site's robots.txt obeyed: the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State, county, city and school district sites, party sites, the Legislative Reference Library, Wikipedia, and the search pages newspapers and broadcasters offer on their own sites (hometownsource.com, wjon.com, thenewsleaders.com, lptv.org, kaxe.org) or their election index pages (dl-online.com, wctrib.com, dglobe.com). Candidates with nothing below are ones for whom no page reached that way stated anything a card may show: Ashley Martin, Brittney Jordan, Krystaline Krumrey, Rollie Nissen, Duane Maupin, Larry P. Magrath, Paul Baillos, Gretchen A. O'Donnell, Josh Edel and Lesley Vavra. For Maupin, Baillos, Krumrey, Vavra, O'Donnell, Magrath and Edel a page was read (a voter's guide, a forum report, or the council or board roster of the body they are running for) and it gave no website and no public office; none of the seven is shown as a member of that body today. Rollie Nissen is on neither the Willmar council page nor the Kandiyohi County Board page today, and the one West Central Tribune story reached says only that he is a candidate for mayor; the Todd County page names the other candidate as the sitting Auditor-Treasurer.

Sites that asked scripts to stay out, refused them or did not answer, and so were not read: seth4mnsos.org and khaiforcarvercounty.com (robots.txt), sheriffwitt.org (a bot check page), isaacschultzmn.com (HTTP 500 on three tries), mncourts.gov (robots.txt: no court page for either judge), cityofdetroitlakes.com and sd41dfl.com (robots.txt), startribune.com (429), trftimes.com (403), the search page of postbulletin.com (robots.txt), ballotpedia.org (an empty challenge page), and jimnashformn.com after its home page (429: its Endorsements page was not read). The Belle Plaine district's old address, belleplaine.k12.mn.us, does not answer; its site is isd716.org. mncd6gop.com now leads to an unrelated site and carvercountydfl.org to a holding page.

Read and left out on purpose: jobs (county staff, campaign staff, legislative staff, a sheriff's office career, law practice), schools, family, church membership and ages; military service; seats on nonprofit boards, a homeowners' association and civic committees; advisory task forces and an ex-officio panel seat; endorsements by people, unions, business and issue groups; and Mustafa Sandhu's 2024 run for the same nonpartisan council. No birth year is given for anyone: the two sitting legislators have theirs in the state roster, and no official, campaign or cited page gave a year for anyone else (an age printed as of one day does not fix a year, and none was taken).

party_support (a key the loader does not read, in the shape parts 0, 6 and 10 use): Patrick Gage, Edina City Council. Two DFL district units publish that he received their "Letter of Support", which each keeps apart from its endorsed candidates (the Senate District 50 DFL under its own heading at the foot of its Endorsed Candidates page, the Senate District 46 DFL on a page of its own). They are not entered as endorsed_by, so that no page calls them endorsements; whether and how they are shown is John's decision.

Party pages read that named nobody in this part, or published no endorsement for them: the SD13 Republicans' site (it names no Senate candidate) and the Benton County Republicans' site (Isaac Schultz is listed among elected officials; no endorsement is stated for him or for Jared Gapinski), the Kanabec County Republicans, the state Republican party's "2026 Republican Nominees" page, the Scott County Republicans' "Endorsed/Recommended Candidates" page (no names in its text), the SD32 and SD37 Republicans, the Minneapolis DFL and the Senate District 34, 37, 43, 55 and 60 DFL sites. The Carver County Republican Party's page names Jim Nash and no candidate for County Commissioner District 5.

For the second reader: (1) Dawanna Witt's past_party item rests on Wikipedia, whose article carries a banner warning that it may hold machine-written text; the claim has a footnote to the Star Tribune of May 15, 2022, whose headline says the same, but that page answered 429 and was not read. No endorsed_by is given for 2026: Wikipedia's article on the 2026 Hennepin County Attorney election cites a Star Tribune story of June 13, 2026 headed "Hennepin County Sheriff Dawanna Witt fails to secure DFL endorsement", and the Senate District 50 DFL's page names an endorsed candidate for County Attorney and none for Sheriff. (2) Mustafa Sandhu: the city's table gives March 7, 2024 as the date appointed, his own site says "Since 2022, I've served for three years"; the city's date is the one entered. (3) Nathan Haase: the county's page for the Attorney's Office names him and nobody else but prints no title, so only the official page is given and no office. (4) Colleen Kinkaid: "Elected: 2026" is what the district prints, although the regular election is in November 2026; the page does not say how the seat was filled. (5) Daniel M. Hawley: the source prints "Daniel Hawley" with no middle initial; it is taken to be him because it reports an appointment to the Ninth Judicial District bench in June 2025 and the 2026 list has one Hawley among that district's judges. (6) Kris Babler's quote and the sentences in his "how" are in the script file that draws his pages (krisbabler.com/assets/index-f98c463a.js); the bare page holds only his name until a browser runs it. (7) Jim Nash is a sitting member: his two Waconia offices are not in the roster, and the review item is the roster's missing start year, as part 6 reported for another member. (8) Rick Greene: the county's page for District #2 (chisagocountymn.gov/919/District-2) prints his board posts back to "Vice Chair, County Board of Commissioners, 2009" but also a home address and telephone, so the County Board page is given as the official page instead. (9) Jenny Peterson: the district's page puts her among two Directors whose terms expire January 4, 2027; the start year is hers. (10) Jared Gapinski: neither the county nor his own site gives the year he joined the County Board.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address was opened again with the kit's User-Agent (robots.txt obeyed); jimnashformn.com and judgestacystennes.com answered 429 to it and were read with WebFetch instead. Three filed websites could not be read and were removed (see "removed"). Rick Greene: the mention of board posts back to 2009 was taken out of "from" (it rests on a page not cited here), and the article's date was corrected to June 18, 2026, updated July 17. The Crosby-Ironton and Mahtomedi school pages are drawn by script; the facts were read in the page's own data. Mustafa Sandhu's "since 2022" is on his site's About page (mustafasandhu.com/about). Jim Nash's review item was checked against member_terms in state_mn.sqlite and the Library's record. The two Letter of Support items for Patrick Gage are confirmed as worded and remain outside endorsed_by.
